docs.title: About aop-cam
docs.text: Adverse outcome pathways as causal activity models.

docs.title: Plan: A GO-CAM-style Schema for the AOP Framework
docs.text: Date: 2026-11-09 Context: Issue #76 proposes framing KE → KER → AOP as a GO-CAM-style causal activity model. This plan compares the three schemas in play and lays out how to draft the new AOP framework schema.

docs.title: 1. The three schemas in play, and what each one is
gocam-py (../gocam-py/src/gocam/schema/gocam.yaml) — the paradigm donor
docs.text:
The GO-CAM schema is small (~950 lines) and its whole design fits in five ideas:

  1. Model = one named causal graph (id, title, taxon, lifecycle status with a rule that production models must have activities, activities, shared objects, provenance, and an optional precomputed query_index).
  2. Activity = one node, defined entirely by its associations: what enables it (enabled_by), what it does (molecular_function), where (occurs_in), what it is part of (part_of), and what it causes (causal_associations).
  3. Association = an abstract class holding evidence[] and provenances[], with a designates_type discriminator. Every edge and every term assignment is an Association subtype. Evidence hangs off every individual assertion, not off the node.
  4. CausalAssociation = predicate (an RO term) + downstream_activity. Initial and terminal nodes are implicit: no incoming edge = initial, no outgoing edge = terminal.
  5. EvidenceItem = ECO term (with a binding enum) + publication reference + supporting objects. Typed TermObject subclasses with id_prefixes constrain what each slot can point at (same idea as SOMA's *Reference classes).

docs.title: linkml-aop (EHS-Data-Standards/linkml-aop) — the data reality
docs.text:
Your hunch is confirmed. The original hand-written schema (linkml_aop.yaml) is archived (September 2026). The current schema, aop_emod_linkml.yaml, is generated from the AOP-Wiki EMOD 3.0 database and is a faithful relational mirror of it: integer ids, join tables (AopToEvent, KeRelationshipToTaxon, ...), admin entities (License, Handbook, OecdStatus), and KER evidence as free-text narrative fields (how_it_works, biological_plausibility, empirical_support, ...). It is not GO-CAM-shaped: no typed causal predicates, no per-assertion evidence objects, causality expressed only as upstream/downstream id pairs plus an adjacency flag.

It does carry two things the other schemas lack:

  • EventComponent: action + object + process per Key Event — AOP-Wiki's proto-EQ decomposition, with ids so components can be shared.
  • The EMOD extension: Assay, Observation, Evidence, BioTargetFamily, TestGuideline — a regulatory-flavored assay layer that overlaps SOMA's territory (see section 5).

docs.title: SOMA's aop_framework.yaml — the current in-between
docs.text: Compositional KE slots (GO process, direction enum, CL/UBERON context), AdverseOutcome as a terminal KeyEvent (recent change), evidence attachable to KEs and KERs, assays linked via informs_on_key_event. Closer in spirit to GO-CAM than linkml-aop is, but ad hoc: relationship_type is a free string, evidence lives on records rather than on assertions, and there is no model lifecycle.

docs.title: 2. The core mapping
docs.text:
GO-CAM New AOP schema Notes Model AopModel One AOP (or AOP network slice) as a named causal graph; adopt lifecycle status enum; taxon applicability Activity KeyEventNode A KE instance in a model enabled_by / molecular_function / occurs_in / part_of ProcessAssociation (GO/MESH), ObjectAssociation, DirectionAssociation (PATO), CellTypeAssociation (CL), AnatomyAssociation (UBERON), LevelAssociation The KE's contextual dimensions, each an Association subtype carrying its own evidence — this is the single biggest paradigm upgrade over current SOMA, where these are bare slot values CausalAssociation CausalAssociation (KER) predicate from an RO causal-predicate enum + downstream_event; keep AOP-Wiki's adjacency, weight of evidence, quantitative understanding as additional slots EvidenceItem EvidenceItem ECO-typed, with publication reference; a SOMA assay becomes the supporting object of an EvidenceItem — formalizing informs_on_key_event as evidence on an assertion initial / terminal activity (implicit) MIE / AO Keep explicit subtyping too (AOP practice names them), but the graph position becomes checkable: an AO with outgoing causal edges is a modeling error a validator can catch TermObject subclasses with id_prefixes SOMA's *Reference pattern Already aligned; converge naming conventions

Mapping AOP-Wiki's edge semantics onto RO: - adjacent → RO:0002412 (immediately causally upstream of), or the regulates variants where direction of effect is curated - non-adjacent → RO:0002411 (causally upstream of) - The 11 AOP-Wiki biological actions → PATO directional qualities (a tiny hand-curated mapping table, done once)

docs.title: 3. What GO-CAM does not cover (the AOP extensions)
docs.text:
These are additions, not deviations:

  1. Direction of change as node state. GO-CAM expresses direction through its relation types; AOPs need "decreased X" as part of the node itself. DirectionAssociation (PATO quality) carries it.
  2. Levels of biological organization. GO-CAM lives at molecular/cellular scale; AOP nodes span molecular → population. A level slot (existing enum), plus UBERON gross anatomy on nodes (GO-CAM has GrossAnatomyAssociation already, so even this is nearly covered).
  3. Outcome grounding. The AO is the terminal node, defined by its composition; optional computed outcome_mappings (HP / MONDO / UPHENO) decorate it (see the outcome-grounding discussion in issue #76).
  4. Regulatory metadata. OECD status, test guidelines — keep as model-level and evidence-level metadata, imported from the linkml-aop vocabulary rather than reinvented.

docs.title: 4. Implementation steps
docs.text:
1. Placement decision (made 2026-11-09). The schema lives in its own repo — this one (EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam) — so that the schema and the graph instances can be imported separately by soma, somamech, and other consumers, each versioned on its own cadence. SOMA imports the schema; instance releases are tagged to the AOP-Wiki snapshot they were built from. EMOD is not a dependency.
  2. Skeleton. AopModel, KeyEventNode, the Association hierarchy (abstract Association with evidence/provenance + the TermAssociation subtypes + CausalAssociation), EvidenceItem, ProvenanceInfo, and the typed term-object/reference classes. Mirror the GO-CAM pattern; do not import gocam.yaml directly (its id prefixes, GO-specific bindings, and gene-product machinery don't transfer).
  3. Causal predicate enum. Minimal RO subset needed by AOPs: causally upstream of, immediately causally upstream of, the positive/negative regulates pair, and causally upstream of with positive/negative effect. Document the AOP-Wiki adjacency mapping.
  4. ETL from the corpus. A loader from data/*.tsv (built 2026-11-09: aops, key_events, key_event_relationships, ke_components, bio_* vocabularies) into instances of the new schema. The 11-row action→PATO mapping table is part of this. Validate by round-tripping the respiratory slice (Aop:148, 411, 424, 425) and comparing against the hand-curated network in the paper's Figure 2.
  5. SOMA integration. An assay's informs_on_key_event link becomes (or is supplemented by) an EvidenceItem on the relevant node association — assays are the experimental support layer of the model. AdverseOutcome stays a KeyEvent subtype; outcome_term evolves into computed outcome_mappings per the uPheno discussion.
  6. Assay layer (decision 2026-11-09): SOMA assays are the evidence layer. EMOD is ignored unless something it covers is modeled better natively here; the only candidates worth absorbing later are test-guideline references and target-family groupings, as small native classes if a use case demands them.
  7. Validation and docs. Examples + counter-examples (an AO with outgoing causal edges; a causal edge with a non-RO predicate; a production model with no events), gen-doc integration, and eventually a query_index analog for precomputed network statistics.

docs.title: 5. Open questions
docs.text:
• How literal to be with GO-CAM? Recommendation: mirror the pattern (Association-with-evidence, typed predicates, model lifecycle), not the vocabulary. A KE is not a molecular Activity; pretending otherwise would confuse both communities.
  • Evidence granularity vs curation burden. Per-assertion evidence is the paradigm's power, but AOP-Wiki data arrives with narrative-level evidence only. Make evidence optional everywhere; let the loader attach what it can (weight-of-evidence labels as model-level annotations) and let new curation do better.
  • One model per AOP, or per network? GO-CAM models merge by shared ontology ids; start with one model per AOP-Wiki AOP (keeps citation clean), and treat networks (like Figure 2) as merged views.
  • Population-level outcomes sit outside every phenotype ontology; composition carries them, mappings stay empty, and that is fine.

docs.title: 6. Suggested first milestone
docs.text: A draft aop_cam.yaml plus a loader that round-trips the four respiratory AOPs from the TSV corpus into valid instances, with the Figure 2 network reproduced by a traversal query. That exercises every design decision above on data the working group already knows by heart.

docs.title: Grounding Receipts: assigning AOP-Wiki text to ontology terms
docs.text:
Every ontology term in an aop_cam instance should be traceable: where the source text came from, what method assigned the term, and how the assignment can be re-verified. The schema supports this natively — every term assignment is an Association carrying its own evidence[] — so receipts live in the data, per assertion, with the canonical mapping records kept as versioned SSSOM files under mappings/.

Receipt classes, strongest claim first:

docs.title: 1. Upstream-asserted (AOP-Wiki supplied the ID)
docs.text: Key event components (process/object ids like GO:0008283), cell terms (CL) and organ terms (UBERON) arrive from AOP-Wiki with ontology ids already assigned. The receipt is the AOP-Wiki record id plus the pinned snapshot (quarterly dump date + SHA-256 of the dump file; nightly dumps are overwritten daily and are not citable). Evidence type: ECO:0000311 (imported information). CI obligation: the label-drift check — the id still exists, is not obsolete, and the stored label still matches a current label or synonym (OAK validation).

docs.title: 2. Mapping-table (deterministic, versioned, SSSOM)
docs.text: Closed vocabularies map through committed SSSOM files — see mappings/aopwiki-action-to-pato.sssom.tsv for the 11 biological actions. Each row carries predicate (exact/closeMatch), mapping_justification, author, date, confidence, and a comment explaining any closeMatch. Evidence type: ECO:0000305 (curator inference used in manual assertion), with the SSSOM record referenced from supporting_objects. CI obligation: the loader may only emit assignments present in the table; an unmapped source value fails the build instead of guessing.

docs.title: 3. Lexical-match (reproducible automation)
docs.text: Free text matching an ontology label or synonym records: the source string verbatim, the matched label or synonym and its scope, the ontology version, and the matcher. Evidence type: ECO:0000203 (automatic assertion). CI obligation: re-run the matcher against the pinned ontology version and require the same answer.

docs.title: 4. Curator/agent judgment (the fuzzy residue)
docs.text: Where no automation is honest, the receipt records the candidate set considered (with scores), the choice, proposer, confirmer, and date — semapv:ManualMappingCuration in SSSOM, alternatives retained. Evidence type: ECO:0000305.

docs.title: 5. Compositional and negative receipts
docs.text: Most adverse outcomes have no precomposed term; the assignment is a composition (process + PATO direction + anatomy), each piece carrying its own class 1–4 receipt. Record the negative receipt too: "searched the uPheno pattern space on date X, version Y; no equivalent above threshold." CI re-runs the search; a future hit surfaces as a proposed outcome_mappings candidate instead of silence.

docs.title: Summary of CI checks
docs.text:
1. Source: quoted AOP-Wiki text occurs in the pinned, hashed dump.
  2. Term: id exists, not obsolete, stored label matches (OAK).
  3. Method: deterministic methods (tables, matchers) reproduce.
  4. Composition: EQ pieces are type-consistent (PATO quality, GO process, UBERON anatomy in the expected branches).

ECO ids verified 2026-11-09 via OAK: ECO:0000311 "imported information", ECO:0000203 "automatic assertion", ECO:0000305 "curator inference used in manual assertion".

docs.title: AOP Causal Activity Models
docs.text:
Adverse Outcome Pathways represented as causal activity models, following the GO-CAM paradigm: an AOP is a model (a named causal graph), each Key Event is a node defined by associations to ontology terms in context, each Key Event Relationship is a typed causal association drawn from the Relation Ontology, and evidence attaches to individual assertions rather than to whole records. The schema mirrors the GO-CAM pattern (Association hierarchy, per-assertion evidence, model lifecycle) without importing its gene-product machinery: a Key Event is not a molecular Activity, and the AOP extensions GO-CAM lacks - direction of change as node state, levels of biological organization up to population, and compositional outcome grounding with optional precomposed-term mappings - are first-class here. Instances can be loaded from AOP-Wiki exports; aopwiki_id slots keep the crosswalk.

URI: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam

Name: aop_cam

docs.title: Class: AopModel
docs.text: One Adverse Outcome Pathway as a causal activity model: a named graph of Key Event nodes connected by typed causal associations. Initial nodes (no incoming causal association) are molecular initiating events; terminal nodes (no outgoing causal association) are adverse outcomes. The event_type on each node states the curator's intent; the graph position is checkable against it.

docs.title: Class: KeyEventNode
docs.text: One Key Event as a node in a causal activity model. The node itself is only an identifier and a label; its meaning comes from its associations - the biological process affected, the object acted on, the direction of change, and the cellular and anatomical context - each of which can carry its own evidence. An adverse outcome is a terminal KeyEventNode: its composition defines it, and outcome_mappings optionally decorate it with precomposed phenotype or disease terms where any exist.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: KeyEventNode
description: 'One Key Event as a node in a causal activity model. The node itself
  is only an identifier and a label; its meaning comes from its associations - the
  biological process affected, the object acted on, the direction of change, and the
  cellular and anatomical context - each of which can carry its own evidence. An adverse
  outcome is a terminal KeyEventNode: its composition defines it, and outcome_mappings
  optionally decorate it with precomposed phenotype or disease terms where any exist.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
attributes:
  id:
    name: id
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    identifier: true
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - AopModel
    - KeyEventNode
    - TermObject
    range: uriorcurie
    required: true
  title:
    name: title
    description: Human-readable name of the key event.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - AopModel
    - KeyEventNode
    range: string
    required: true

    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - AopModel
    - KeyEventNode
    range: string
  event_type:
    name: event_type
    description: 'The curator-asserted role of this node in the pathway. Must be consistent
      with graph position: a molecular_initiating_event has no incoming causal associations,
      an adverse_outcome has no outgoing ones.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: EventTypeEnum
  level_of_biological_organization:
    name: level_of_biological_organization
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: LevelOfBiologicalOrganizationEnum
  process:
    name: process
    description: The biological process this key event perturbs.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: ProcessAssociation
    inlined: true
  object:
    name: object
    description: The biological object (molecule, cell, structure) acted on.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: ObjectAssociation
    inlined: true
  direction:
    name: direction
    description: The direction of change, as a PATO quality.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: DirectionAssociation
    inlined: true
  occurs_in_cell_type:
    name: occurs_in_cell_type
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: CellTypeAssociation
    inlined: true
  occurs_in_anatomy:
    name: occurs_in_anatomy
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: GrossAnatomyAssociation
    inlined: true
  causal_associations:
    name: causal_associations
    description: The causal associations that flow out of this node. A node with none
      is terminal in the model; a node no other node points at is initial.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: CausalAssociation
    multivalued: true
    inlined: true
    inlined_as_list: true
  outcome_mappings:
    name: outcome_mappings
    description: 'For adverse outcome nodes: precomposed terms equivalent or close
      to this outcome''s compositional definition, where any exist (HPO phenotype,
      MONDO disease, or uPheno class). A decoration for discovery, not the definition;
      candidates can be generated by matching the node''s entity+quality composition
      against uPheno''s pattern space.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    rank: 1000
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - KeyEventNode
    range: uriorcurie
    multivalued: true
    pattern: ^(HP:\d{7}|MONDO:\d{7}|UPHENO:\d+)$
  provenances:
    name: provenances
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam
    owner: KeyEventNode
    domain_of:
    - AopModel
    - KeyEventNode
    - Association
    - EvidenceItem
    range: ProvenanceInfo
    multivalued: true
    inlined: true
    inlined_as_list: true

docs.title: aop_cam
docs.text:
Adverse Outcome Pathways represented as causal activity models, following the GO-CAM paradigm: an AOP is a model (a named causal graph), each Key Event is a node defined by associations to ontology terms in context, each Key Event Relationship is a typed causal association drawn from the Relation Ontology, and evidence attaches to individual assertions rather than to whole records. The schema mirrors the GO-CAM pattern (Association hierarchy, per-assertion evidence, model lifecycle) without importing its gene-product machinery: a Key Event is not a molecular Activity, and the AOP extensions GO-CAM lacks - direction of change as node state, levels of biological organization up to population, and compositional outcome grounding with optional precomposed-term mappings - are first-class here. Instances can be loaded from AOP-Wiki exports; aopwiki_id slots keep the crosswalk.

URI: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/aop-cam

docs.title: Slot: aopwiki_ker_id
docs.text: AOP-Wiki identifier for this relationship (e.g. "Relationship:2555").

docs.title: Slot: causal_associations
docs.text: The causal associations that flow out of this node. A node with none is terminal in the model; a node no other node points at is initial.

docs.title: Slot: direction
docs.text: The direction of change, as a PATO quality.

docs.title: Slot: downstream_event
docs.text: The key event node this edge points to.

docs.title: Slot: event_type
docs.text: The curator-asserted role of this node in the pathway. Must be consistent with graph position: a molecular_initiating_event has no incoming causal associations, an adverse_outcome has no outgoing ones.

docs.title: Slot: evidence_level
docs.text: Weight of evidence for this relationship, as curated.

docs.title: Slot: id
docs.text: A unique identifier.

docs.title: Slot: key_events
docs.text: All Key Event nodes in this model.

docs.title: Slot: label
docs.text: The human-readable label of the term, as given by its ontology.

docs.title: Slot: models
docs.text: The models in this collection.

docs.title: Slot: object
docs.text: The biological object (molecule, cell, structure) acted on.

docs.title: Slot: oecd_status
docs.text: OECD endorsement status, carried over from AOP-Wiki.

docs.title: Slot: outcome_mappings
docs.text: For adverse outcome nodes: precomposed terms equivalent or close to this outcome's compositional definition, where any exist (HPO phenotype, MONDO disease, or uPheno class). A decoration for discovery, not the definition; candidates can be generated by matching the node's entity+quality composition against uPheno's pattern space.

docs.title: Slot: predicate
docs.text: The RO causal relation for this edge.

docs.title: Slot: process
docs.text: The biological process this key event perturbs.

docs.title: Slot: reference
docs.text: The publication the evidence comes from (PMID, DOI, or AOPWIKI page).

docs.title: Slot: snapshot_date
docs.text: Date of the AOP-Wiki snapshot these models were derived from, when applicable. Nightly dumps are overwritten daily, so cite a quarterly dump date wherever possible.

docs.title: Slot: source
docs.text: Where this content came from, e.g. "AOPWiki" for converted content or a curation project name for new assertions.

docs.title: Slot: status
docs.text: Lifecycle status of the model.

docs.title: Slot: stressors
docs.text: Chemical or physical stressors known to trigger this pathway, as ontology term references where possible.

docs.title: Slot: supporting_objects
docs.text: Identifiers of supporting records, such as SOMA assay instances or database entities.

docs.title: Slot: taxa
docs.text: Taxa this model is asserted to apply to.

docs.title: Slot: term
docs.text: The ontology term this association assigns.

docs.title: Slot: type
docs.text: Auto-populated association type discriminator.
